doc.title: Ametria Dock interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 4, 2019

title: 'You Are My Sunshine' as a teaching song
summary: Dock loves the song and uses it with advanced singers, reworking it in Gospel, jazz or pop styles.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Well I know you have a busy day and I appreciate you taking — there’s one just anecdote to share. Yesterday you were talking about early on you got in a position where the producer or whatever said, “So sing.” Right?

And I’m thinking to myself what did she sing? And I play on occasion at homes for retired adults or so forth or nursing homes on occasion. And one song I always play is “You Are My Sunshine.” And I’ll be darned if that wasn’t the song. I said I never would have thought of that.

Wow. I use that all the time. It’s like one of my faves. You know I love the way that that song just brings joy and makes me feel happy. It’s a cute song, it’s a happy song, but — and I know any time you hear that song it just makes you feel good, right? But sometimes © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

when I have a very advanced singer who’s wanting to learn a different way to approach the way that they do what they do, I use “You Are My Sunshine” and I make it a little more complicated. And it’s like, it feels light and bright, so I may make it feel more Gospel or make it feel more jazz, or make it feel more pop. So I just use that because it’s such a happy song to me but you can do so many things with it.
